title: Putin Warns the West About a Small Russian Territory Called Kaliningrad
summary:
Imagine a piece of Russia that isn't touching Russia. It's called Kaliningrad, and it sits between Poland and Lithuania. It's a bit bigger than the U.S. state of Connecticut.

On Thursday, Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke at a meeting in Moscow called the Valdai Forum. He said the world is in a dangerous moment. He warned Western countries not to push Russia over Kaliningrad.

Putin said Russia would use "all the weapons at our country's disposal" — including nuclear weapons — if Kaliningrad is attacked. Nuclear weapons are the most powerful bombs ever made.

But Putin also said Russia has no plans to attack any European country. He said Russia wants to live peacefully with others.

NATO is a group of 32 countries, including the U.S., Britain, and France, that promise to defend each other. This week, NATO said Russia sent it a note warning about nuclear weapons if NATO tried to cut Kaliningrad off from Russia.

NATO's leader, Mark Rutte, replied that NATO is a defensive alliance — it doesn't start fights. He said nuclear threats don't help.

Putin also said he is open to meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping if they agree on what to talk about first.
why_it_matters: Kaliningrad is far from most kids' homes, but when leaders talk about nuclear weapons, people everywhere get worried — and it shows how one small piece of land can become one of the most dangerous spots in the world.

background_read: Kaliningrad (a small Russian region on the Baltic Sea between Poland and Lithuania) used to belong to Germany and was called Königsberg; after World War II it became part of the Soviet Union, and today it belongs to Russia even though it does not touch Russia.

NATO (the North Atlantic Treaty Organization — a group of 32 countries, including the U.S., Britain and France, that promise to defend each other) was created after World War II to keep its members safe.

Vladimir Putin (Russia's president) spoke at the Valdai Forum, a yearly meeting in Moscow where he answers questions about world affairs — and nuclear weapons, the most powerful bombs ever made, were part of his warning.
Article_Structure: WHO: Russian President Vladimir Putin, NATO and its leader Mark Rutte, and U.S. President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping.

WHAT: Putin warned the West not to push Russia over Kaliningrad and said Russia would use any weapon, even nuclear, if Kaliningrad is attacked — while also saying Russia has no plans to attack Europe.
WHERE: Kaliningrad, the piece of Russia sitting between Poland and Lithuania, and the Valdai Forum meeting in Moscow.

WHY: NATO says Russia warned that nuclear weapons might be used if NATO cut Kaliningrad off, and Putin wants the West to take that threat seriously, while NATO answers that it is only a defensive alliance.

perspectives.description: Russia says Western countries are pushing it, and warns it would use 'all the weapons at our country's disposal' to defend Kaliningrad, while insisting it has no plans to attack Europe.
NATO's leader Mark Rutte replied that NATO is a defensive alliance that does not start fights, and that nuclear threats do not help anyone.

Analysts note that Kaliningrad has been a tense spot since World War II, because Russian weapons there sit right next to NATO countries — and talking, not threatening, is the only way to calm things down.
